subjects.label: Hoche's western counter-insurgency and pacification
subjects.meaning: General Hoche's military concentration, guerrilla suppression, victory at Quiberon, and combined coercive and conciliatory pacification of the west.
subjects.stance: Hoche’s pacification combined overwhelming and adaptive force with toleration and control of republican abuses. Treating this as repression alone erases why peasant support dwindled; earlier retaliatory brutality had helped prolong resistance.

before.evidence_summary: Condé’s surviving regiments entered imperial service as the main exception to émigré military disintegration.
Describes the 1795-1796 scheme, British agents, attempts to win Pichegru, Austrian reluctance, and Louis XVIII's unwelcome presence.
The remaining émigré military force under Condé depended on Austrian service and could not act independently.
before.reconciliation_rationale: Retain this inspected final-release page claim in the named successor treatment; the chapter proposal used fewer illustrative pages,which is not grounds to lose this source-supported facet.
